reasoning: White cottony mycelium with dark sclerotia on the exterior of the stem at the soil line/crown is the classic presentation of Southern Blight (Sclerotium rolfsii). The lesion location, surface mycelial fan, and sclerotia on the stem exterior match this disease. Sclerotinia is less likely as its sclerotia are typically larger, more elongated, and found inside the stem cavity.
